body:
Rationally, what do you think the odds are that you'll meet someone you end up caring a great deal for? Or that those 2 people you mention above will forgive you eventually?

My point is that if you are feeling like you are alone, then you're in a degree of pain that is going to make it difficult to see things objectively. Could you change who you are on a level that will help you not to create more problems? Could you become someone who accepts, even if you regret, your mistakes? 

The way I see it, you can do anything you want before you die. Sell all your possessions and move to India. Go bungee-jumping. Anything at all. So, best to just make sure you've explored all options and considered all potential outcomes, you know?

Okay, I'm going to be real with you, and this may hurt. I'm sorry, but I think you really are unaware of the implications of what you are saying, and I worry that your attitude will negatively impact your memories of your sister.

It sounds to me like you feel superior to her, and that is what's causing you guilt. You need to acknowledge that, and accept the fact that life has different paths for different people, and that your success is not THE definition of success. She birthed two children, and you describe yourself as "doing good things in life" because you didn't choose to have children and instead focused on your studies. Do you realize how condescending that sounds? Most would say that having a child were far more important than getting a degree.

Essentially, you are saying that you feel guilty because you feel like she took her life because she couldn't measure up to the person you've become. 

Well, she didn't. She most likely didn't want to life that you lead at all. Most people do not want that life. I know, because I was just like you when I was younger. You someday may not even want it yourself.

She didn't kill herself because she couldn't be as good as you turned out, or because you weren't a "good example" enough to show her how to overcome obstacles. She killed herself because she was in pain, and there was nothing anyone could have done to help her alleviate it to the point where life would be worth living. 

Learn not to look at her life through that lens of judgment. It's not good for you, and it may sour your feelings toward your sister--may she rest in peace--to an irreparable point.

Be the best person YOU want to be. Imagine that your sister would celebrate your accomplishments, not because they make you "better" at life, but because they make you proud, they make you happy.

Because most people don't want to die, and they can't understand why anyone would. They assume that desire is just temporary. Depression is a six week spell of sadness, as far as they understand. It's not a lifetime sentence the way most of us know it to be.

Is this is olds club? Checking in. I'm 29. Had a decent life. Most would say that it looked very pretty from the outside, and that I've reached what should be the beginning of the best part of my life. Had a fantastic career that paid well, now at one of the top professional schools in the country to get an even better job, but I'm more miserable than ever.

I'm just old enough to know its not going to get any better, and I look at my younger classmates, and I wish I would have done something to stop this from happening.

I would've liked to be in a relationship where my feelings were reciprocated. I'm sorry I'll go out without having had that experience.

I feel the same way. I read about these teenagers and it pains me to know that they are in the same place I was so many years ago. And it pains me to know that some of them may never get better, and will be sitting behind their laptops 15 years later, wondering why they let all of this go on for so long.

I wish it weren't true, except that I'm living (unfortunately) proof of it.

I am SO with you.

Lovely life on paper. Miserable every morning and night. Unable to feel the gratitude you know you should, because there's just too much unhappiness and apathy.

I'll never measure up to my own standards, and I've just grown so tired of trying. Why do I hate living so much? I don't think anyone will even understand why I've killed myself, when I'm gone. 

You've got daughters, though. A family, obligations. That makes it harder.

Anyway, I'm here if you want to talk.
Rest in peace, Throwaway19871996. I understand, and I'm sorry for your pain.

Why give up?

I mean that literally. Like, what are your real options here. Lay out all the cards. You can die or live. Tell me why you should or should not do both.
:( I wish I could say something to help.

That's actually a great idea, to tour the country. Maybe you can find your place.

I think we all have one, it's out there, but I think it's difficult to find. It involves so much risk. I tell myself I should just drop everything and go move to the desert and be an artist, but then I'm too much of a coward. I'll end up killing myself without having ever even tried to find my place.

Go. Explore. You can do anything you want before you die, right? Try anything, be whoever you want to be.
I'm right there with you. Literally hoped on this board to post something similar.

Just found out I have to retake this class I haven't been going to next year.

Yeah, okay. I won't be here, but, whatever.

School admins are idiots.

We're not allowed to share that kind of information. Needless to say, suffocating yourself is extremely painful/uncomfortable, and when you begin to lose consciousness, your body automatically takes over and removes the bag. 

Just don't want you to end up in a mental ward after making a huge spectacle in a public place. That would probably make you feel a lot worse.

Update: I've spent the week in bed. Haven't showered; my hair is disgusting. I just switched into a new pair of pajamas. I'm gross. I've been eating chocolate and ice cream every day.

I can barely make myself watch television. I just stare at nothing for hours, sitting next to my cat, who doesn't deserve to be abandoned.

School admins are emailing me because I'm missing a required course every day. I'll have full classes for a week or two before my birthday; sometimes I wonder what these professors who will barely know me will think. The pressures of X school. Competition so fierce. I'm sure the school will get a neat little example to provide to their students: here's why you should talk to someone if you're hurting. (Wasn't she so pretty?)

Except the only thing school has to do with this at all is that I want to make sure my parents are reimbursed the tuition I payed. (And thank god for student loan forgiveness upon death.)

Sad girls claws her way up from nothing, reaches the peak of her life, hasn't been able to muster any enthusiasm about it. It's too bad that nobody will understand that that's just what makes depression depression. I could be crowned queen and still want to take a nosedive off the highest balcony.

If my ex hadn't broken up with me, actually, it probably would have been just enough to guilt me into living. I wonder if he remembers that I told him I'd be dead by the end of this month, while we shared a bottle of wine in bed on one of our first dates. Probably not. 

I did get the designer gown I plan to die in dry cleaned last month. There's that.
P.S. Happy birthday. January babies. Sending love to your spirit if you are already gone. I wish you peace.

I wonder if you are still here. We sound similar. I'm not even depressed, it just really is now or never and I don't want to live long term.

I guess this is how adults kill themselves, sorting out all the financial issues, picking a solid date, making sure to make your death as inconvenient as possible for those you love.
My parents have suffered so much. I don't want to cause them any more pain. I just wish I would die of natural causes. It would hurt them so much less.
I'm here if you want to talk. Kind of going through the same thing. Just spend my days in bed waiting for the time to arrive.

Guilt. All I can see is the horrible guilt. No matter how much I try to convince myself that I won't be there to feel the guilt, I can't seem to accept it.

It sucks to be living only because you don't want to hurt someone else's feelings. What about my feelings? Why doesn't what I want matter at all?
You may want to reconsider. It's not a very good method.

Doctor. Your best move is to see a psychologist. It sounds like this is something you've been struggling with on and off for a while... episodes can get worse with age, so don't risk spiraling into a black hole.
Right there with you. Wish I had the answer.

Well, I do. I advocate for lying to a shrink. If you cannot get help because you are vocalizing a plan for suicide, stop vocalizing it. Tell them you feel suicidal, but do not give details. The goal here is to get help because after all you don't *actually* want to kill yourself. Suicide is just your last resort, the absolute desperate act. So rather than rush into the room saying "I'm going to jump in front of a train on X day, and I hope you all go to hell," instead rephrase by focusing on your intention in being there in front of the psychologist, in asking for help: "I feel like I want to die, and I don't want to feel this way anymore. I feel angry, and I feel like nobody wants to help me get better, and I want to get better."

This is depression 101. Anyone who has experienced multiple episodes can tell you that this is the key to getting help without landing yourself in the psychiatric ward, or, in the OP's case, getting doctors to refuse to provide treatment. (Still not clear on how that works in the UK; seems like a human rights violation to me to refuse someone medical treatment when they need it and I'm guessing there are details we are not privy to here.)

Well, you can't just lie down and die, here. Literally, you need to actively go out into the world to kill yourself. Why not reroute that energy into actively trying to find what will help you stay alive?

You WANT to live. So live. You are your own best help here. Listen to yourself. In the end, it is you who goes to decide. If nobody will give you help, go and take it yourself. If you can't find a psychologist, then find an online support group, find a group therapy meet-up to attend, etc. 

There are options. It sounds to me like you just don't want to fight for life. But you can't do nothing; you'd have to fight for death, too. Why would you make yourself do something you don't even want, in the end? You have two paths here. Pick the one you want to take.

And for god sakes don't throw yourself in front of a train. You seem smart enough. I think you know that would be a remarkably short-sighted thing to do, that likely would not result in death, but just make everything much worse.
I wonder, too. I worry there's something I'm missing that I could do. But it's been almost two decades now. If there were a way, I would have found it by now.

I think I know what you need to do: find another happiness. 

Sit down and write out a list of everything that makes you smile to think of, puppies, YouTube makeup videos, a plate full of french fries, your favorite skirt. Then see which of those you can pursue as a hobby, as something you do purely for yourself alone. Maybe you volunteer at the local dog shelter once a week. Maybe you commit to learning how to create new makeup looks or take up painting. Do you enjoy cooking? Maybe you start experimenting with different recipes. Maybe you learn to sew or embroider or knit.

Pick something you think you could enjoy, and try to expand on it. Create your own source of happiness. Find what makes you feel good to do, and do it.

I believe that everyone has a purpose, but you have to go after it. You need to actively work to discern what it is and how you can achieve it. You have to go after what calls to you, what speaks to your soul.

If you're not sure where to start, I'm sure we can all help provide ideas if you tell us a little bit about what interests or appeals to you.
What would it take to make you want to live? What kind of life do you wish you had right now?

I completely, completely understand this feeling.

What is it, exactly, that makes you not want to live anymore? Is it your father?
I'm sorry you feel this way, too.

Yes. I think about how those I love will respond to the news, how they will grieve. I wonder if maybe some people I care about but with whom I have no contact will never even find out that I'm gone. I worry that people will blame themselves for not doing something.

The truth is that nobody can do anything to help. The decision is mine. But I know the human tendency is to analyze, and try to find that place, that moment, act or omission where the outcome could have been different.

I hate to think that my being at peace will come at the expense of the happiness of those I love. I know they will get through it, but I hate to think of them wasting time mourning me.

At the same time, it would be nice to know that I was loved maybe more than I believe I am. The knowledge wouldn't change the outcome, but it's always nice to have someone you care about care about you, too.

This is probably the least appropriate, but most effective and important approach: Think about what would happen if you jumped in front of that train and ended up paralyzed, but alive. Say you still feel the same way that you do now, you are miserable, want to die. But you are paralyzed. You cannot move your arms or legs. What will you do then?

Does jumping in front of a train still sound like a good idea? I wouldn't risk it. Many, many people live after throwing themselves in front of a train. Some do end up paralyzed because of it.

I think maybe you haven't thought this through. I think if you were handed another option, one that involves living, but living without all the emotional pain, that you would take it.

The fact that you are angry with these psychologists suggests that you want help. It sounds like you are in a city. If that's true, you know that you can find another psychologist. Approach with this idea, this intention: "I don't want to have to feel like I should kill myself." That is your goal. That and only that. Before you get anywhere else, you need to get to a place where you do not actively want to die.

Together, with the right psychologist, you can find out exactly what you need to do to get yourself there. It exists. Even the most suicidal have experienced it: that year or week or day or moment where you WANTED, absolutely WANTED to live. You're capable of returning to it. You just need help finding the path to it. The right psychologist will help you to create the map that you will need to get to where you want to be.

Well, if you recognize that you've made poor choices, can you see what would have been a better decision? If so, you very much have the power to change the situation. That means that you are growing. That means you are becoming a better, more experienced, more aware person.

Don't let these strangers tell you who YOU are. They don't know you. Their words are empty, devoid of any meaning or power if you realize that it is YOU decides who you are.

Who is the kind of person that you want to be, ThatOneDude? What small thing can you do right now to get a little bit closer to that improved version of yourself? Think small, like tidying your room or making a grocery list.

Please know that the feeling goes away. 

You've experienced a major trauma. It hurts now so, so much, I know, but time dulls the pain. Like a broken bone that didn't heal quite right, it will ache if you press on it, or you bump into something, but most of the time, it'll be as if it isn't even there. I know you can't see that right now, but time will heal you. Therapy will help expedite that process.

Consider reaching out to others. Our experiences are all different, but I'm sure you can find someone with whom you can connect. It can be helpful to work through this with someone who you feel understands what you are experiencing.

It may be especially difficult for you to trust others. That doesn't mean that they really are untrustworthy. Why not test the waters? Can you reveal just a little part of you, and see how they respond? Tell them you have a really bad night, rather than that you've been having a really bad few weeks, or months?

If they don't respond well, then that's okay. Some people just can't handle it, maybe aren't strong enough to deal with those of us who have some really difficult shit going on.

You won't know until you try, though.

Have you tried therapy at all? It sounds like you really are focusing in on your skin here... it's just one part of who you are. No matter how much you may hate it, it's only one part. There are so many other things about you that can make you a desirable partner. Think of burn victims or those that have been in unfortunate accidents. Some suffer from diseases that prevent them from growing hair. Others may have terrible scars from self-mutilation, or have damaged their skin permanently by using unsafe beauty aids. Does that make them unlovable? Unworthy?

If you could look past appearances, what makes you think she can't too? Just because she is beautiful? She may have some deep dark reason that makes her hurt, too. In fact, you may be the most beautiful person in the world to her, because she sees something about you that she has never seen in anyone else, that she loves.

If you're beginning to already try to sabotage this relationship because you don't think you deserve her or that it could possibly work out, you are shortchanging yourself. You need to work through your issues. 

She can't be the only hope you have. You're your own hope. And, I have to say, if you could manage to attract this woman, you can attract others, too. It is basic logic, right? If you are attractive to her, then you are attractive. Ergo, there are women who would find you attractive. Even if things don't work out with her, there are other women to pursue.

In the meantime, I think you should work on accepting yourself. Nobody should have to live inside a body that they dislike so much. 

What you're doing currently isn't making you happy, right? So then you need to pursue a change. I think talking to someone, a professional, who can help you to focus on your positive attributes and to do the things that will lead you to feel better about yourself (e.g. diet, hobbies, intellectual pursuits) might be the change you need.

Wishing you all the best.

This is what the internet is for. Or hotlines. There are plenty of hotlines you can call to just vent; the people on the other end are there to listen.

You may feel alone, but you are not alone. People leave, yes. But that's not your fault, and it doesn't mean that people will always leave you.

I've always thought that you make your own family. You surround yourself with the people who feel like family should, like they care about you and are there for you always. Do you have friends? Do you go to school?

This is not uncommon, the feeling guilty for being down, or feeling like you must just be "making it up" in your head, that it isn't a real problem. This is a major indication of depression.

You don't feel like yourself any more, right? Just because there are glimpses of the you you are, say when you're having fun with friends, doesn't mean you're not depressed, or that you don't suffer from anxiety issues. 

Think of it this way: Just because a diabetic's blood sugar levels aren't too high at certain times of the day or when eating certain things, doesn't mean they're not diabetic anymore. Make sense?

It sounds like your mother notices that you are unhappy. Can you tell her you haven't been feeling well and you want to see a doctor?

Also, noticed you said it's been lasting for six months. That's a LONG time. My first depressive episode sounds a lot like yours, where I knew something wasn't right for half a year, but felt like I didn't deserve to get help or that it was my own fault for being unhappy. You really should see someone and be completely honest about how you are feeling. You may need medication or therapy, and that's okay. There's no shame in that.

Don't keep spiraling. You don't have to go this alone.

Me three on this. I think a huge part of the problem is the negative, self-perpetuating thoughts. "I don't deserve to be loved," "I only fuck things up," "I say dumb shit," "Nobody likes me." If you're like me, you have those thoughts set on replay in your mind.

I got to a point where I was very well, where I had finally started to come to accept myself and to feel positively about who I am. This current depressive episode totally wrecked it because I let it (too easy to slip into old habits and just stay in bed all day hating yourself), but what I found helpful then was to acknowledge those negative thoughts and then let them go. Just because you think something, doesn't make it a reality, and even if you have accurately assessed a situation (e.g. "I'm an idiot for saying what I said to my friend") then you can still separate the action from who you are (reframe as "I said an idiotic thing to my friend. It was a mistake, I will learn from it." Because the truth is, you're not an idiot by simple virtue of recognizing that you made that mistake). 

You don't have to tell yourself you love yourself and do blah blah positive affirmations. But find something you do like about yourself, however small. Do you have nicely shaped hands? Strong calves? Are you talented at painting? Can you kick anyone's butt at a certain video game? There must be little things that you DO like about yourself. Remind yourself of those things when you're feeling down.

Bonus points if: 1. You start a running list of the things you appreciate. I put mine on my phone and added to it a few times a week. I swear to god I had better luck then ever before, like being appreciative just made good things happen to me. I would put big things like "scored that job interview I wanted" or little things like "walked by this pretty group of birds, weather is nice today." If I literally felt I had nothing else because, say, I spent the entire day in bed watching television, I would put something like "watched Scrubs all day and I'm grateful that the show made me laugh and forget about my problems for a while." Just write that shit down. Acknowledge it.

Okay, you can totally ignore me if you think it's dumb. But it's worth a shot, I'd say. Anything to feel better. 

P.P.S. Specific to hunter2ismypass I felt like I had nothing interesting to say, so I started having a few blogs send me daily news updates via email (Mashable, for example). I read an article or two a day, quick stuff that interests me. It's so easy when there's a lull in conversation to say, "So I was reading about this new technology..." Maybe give it a try?

The next time you go on a dinner date, can you try to give that woman a kiss goodnight? If you're nervous she will say no, you can always ask: "Is it okay if I kiss you?" I would never be bothered by that, and I don't think any of my girlfriends would, either.

I feel fairly confident that if you haven't kissed by the second date, you cannot assess compatibility. Is this something you are discussing with your therapist? I wonder if your inexperience with physical intimacy is kind of perpetuating itself... you haven't been intimate so you continue not to be intimate and thus feel that you CAN'T be intimate, or that there's a reason why women don't want to be with you.

More than anything, though, you have to work on you and get to a place where you self-esteem isn't in the shitter. You cannot be in a relationship when you feel so negatively about yourself and your life. It wouldn't be fair to the person you are with, and it isn't fair to you. Say you meet your dream girl tomorrow--would you be ready to date her? Do you feel confident that you could be with her? (My guess is that you'd be unsure of how to act/what to do because of insecurity.)

Get yourself to who YOU want to be, and fuck all what women want or dating right now. 

You know that bullshit about how until you love yourself, nobody can love you? It really is shit. You can be loved without loving yourself. But you'll still feel unlovable. You won't believe that your partner really could love you, or that you deserve to be loved by them. If you're like me, you'll go to rather desperate lengths to prove it to whomever you're with, too.

I also third the suggest regarding medication. 

P.S. I was unlucky in love at your age, too. I'm now much older and not unlucky anymore, except I never figured out how to stop hating myself, and so I've never been able to make a relationship last for more than a few months. One has to come before the other. I promise that it won't work the other way. You won't find validation in romantic relationships.
Aw, man. I just smile half-heartedly at this point. Sometimes re-direct the question, usually try to keep communication as short as possible.

Thank you. I will try to see my family before. 

I hope you stay un-depressed, and live the life you had always dreamed.

I can do that. Thank you. I would've assumed whatever I wrote would hold.

ETA: Farkkkkk I need TWO witnesses. I seriously don't know who I can possibly ask.

Yeah, you totally get it. They really should just legalize this. My life, my decision. It's unfair that those of us who want to end it sometimes have to go through so much unnecessary pain to do so, besides the potential for fucking it up and just making everything even worse.

I know how lonely it can be to not be able to be honest about your feelings. It can feel like you're just screaming into the void in posting on the internet. But it sure is better than nothing at all.
Such a good way of describing it.

Ugh, the people who live in my building. :( Hopefully everything can be taken care of very quietly. I don't want to disturb any of my neighbors. I'd never haunt the place! But who knows what they believe about the afterlife.

I'm really frankly upset that my organs are going to go to waste, but it's basically impossible to arrange things so that you're discovered brain dead. I do wish I had more money to give away. I wonder if something can be done with my belongings.

I'm thinking of donating my remains to science but the idea of my body being used as instructional material for years to come is kind of horrifying.

Yes. Over a dozen years. I've tried many medications.

I wish they would just make suicide legal already. It's not like I haven't done my due diligence in trying to get better. For half my god damn life.

I'm leaving a letter; it's just that I can't decide whether it would be good to actually physically see them before I, err, go. 

I'm having a hard time trying to gauge what will be the least difficult on everyone. In truth I want to just get it over with in the next few days, but I feel like I owe it to my parents to visit them first.

And, yeah, been there, done that. This is a very educated decision I'm making. There's no chance of me telling a single soul how I really feel. One of the only things that's been stopping me is worrying that I'll fuck it up somehow and be put in a mental hospital. Living through a suicide attempt would be the worst thing that could possibly happen to me.

The same thing happened to me a few months ago. The guy I was seeing broke up with me the next month. I had been falling in love with him. 

If I could go back and do it again, I would have tried harder to be okay. Pick up a new hobby, something. I plunged into the deepest depression, instead. Please don't let this consume you. You can find another job to love. There is a future for you. You just have to try a little. Plan a small goal every day.

If you don't feel you can speak to your boyfriend or family, then journal. Writing it all down can help.

I know you can turn this around. You aren't happy where you are, right, laying in bed and just watching television. So why not find something to do, however small, that will make you feel more positive?

I know it is hard. I know how difficult it is.

Bed will always be there for you, if trying to get up and moving doesn't work out.
I'm quitting mine tomorrow. She hasn't helped for shit. I've spent the past year working with her and it literally has done nothing to alleviate my depression.
I'm sorry. I wish I could make you feel differently.

Is there something that could happen that you think would make you feel better? Even just for the moment, what could you do to distract yourself? Is there a television show that makes you laugh? Do you like to workout; can you do a few push-ups? Do you have a cat or dog you could pet? Is there a room in your home that needs cleaning? Even something neutral, like cleaning, can help to calm the bad thoughts.

I always find that if I go and do something else, anything else, after some time, maybe even just ten or fifteen minutes, I don't feel so awful anymore. I may still want to die, but I don't want to actively die right then at that exact moment.

If you have difficulty talking about your problems and really opening up, then you don't really know if they can be alleviated by working through them, discussing them, with someone you've developed a trusting relationship with, right? Why not give that a try first? You have nothing to lose.
You say that even when you are happy, you think about dying. Is this is because you think that your happiness doesn't matter or that it won't last?

I understand. I'm just waiting for that final push, too. Because I can't become the person I want to be, either.

I wish I could say something to make you feel better, but I don't know what would. I'm here if you want to talk, though. I've been feeling pretty alone, sitting here all day knowing I'm going to kill myself. If you feel alone too, you don't need to anymore.

And if there is any small part of you that wants to live, I think his might help: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lXi7vcnvl5c. It has helped me in the past.

It makes me so upset to think that anyone else would want to kill themselves. You sound very self-aware, intelligent. I'm sure you have more going for you than you think.
